claims.text: Thermal aging at 600–800 °C promotes chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
As-synthesized HfNbTaTiZr is a random solid solution with minimal pre-existing short-range order.
Aging at 600–800 °C can induce short-range order without significant grain growth or precipitation.
The induced short-range order forms nanoscale regions with locally altered lattice parameters.
Short-range-ordered regions have thermal-expansion coefficients that differ locally from the surrounding alloy.
Local lattice-spacing and thermal-expansion mismatches generate heterogeneous internal stresses.
Short-range order alters dislocation mobility in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Short-range order can enhance edge-dislocation mobility while reducing screw-dislocation double-kink nucleation.
In HfNbTaTiZr, SRO-induced internal stresses hinder or enhance glide and kink nucleation.
SRO-induced internal stresses modify the elastic response of HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed SRO mechanism unifies the alloy's creep behavior, cold-rolling microhardness changes, and temperature-dependent elastic moduli.
Relative to the as-synthesized alloy, aged HfNbTaTiZr will have a modified creep activation response.
Relative to the as-synthesized alloy, aged HfNbTaTiZr may have lower screw-dislocation double-kink nucleation rates.
Aged HfNbTaTiZr will show increased microhardness during cold rolling relative to the as-synthesized baseline.
Aged HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit measurable deviations in elastic moduli, especially near 1250 °C.
The proposed mechanism is significant over 293 K to 1250 °C.
Grain refinement or processing-induced defects could alternatively contribute to the observed mechanical behavior.
Samples with identical processing and grain structure, differing only in aging-induced SRO, constitute the intended controlled comparison.
